title: StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a real-valued objective that may be nonconvex. The public starting point and gap bound satisfy f(x₀) − inf f ≤ Δ, with Δ ≥ 0. The infimum need not be attained.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.Instance, spec.valid and the inequality ∀ x, f q.x0 − f x ≤ q.Δ in spec.admissible.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns one vector g(x, ξ) with mean ∇f(x). Each call uses a fresh independent seed with the same law, including repeated calls at x. The parameters E, Ω, x₀, L₁, L₂, L₃, σ, Δ and ε are public. The objective, response map and sampling law are hidden. The oracle exposes only the returned vector.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, spec.Reply and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: At every x, the centered squared error is integrable and E‖g(x, ξ) − ∇f(x)‖² ≤ σ². The public bound permits σ = 0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.valid and the centered second-moment conditions in spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel measurable structure.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The objective is C³. Its gradient, Hessian and third derivative are globally Lipschitz with respective public bounds L₁, L₂ and L₃, all strictly positive. The derivative bounds use induced operator norms. These smoothness conditions apply to f alone.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.valid and the ContDiff and three Lipschitz conditions in spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns a measurable point X in E with integrable gradient norm. The criterion uses the first power of ‖∇f(X)‖.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E‖∇f(X)‖ ≤ ε for the public tolerance ε > 0. The expectation covers both the algorithm seed and the oracle seeds. The oracle-call budget is a fixed cap on each run.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/Template.lean, OracleTemplate.Convergence and executeWithTrace.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation pairs a gradient-only, bounded-variance oracle with separate global controls on the Hessian and third derivative of the objective. Those higher-order bounds are available to the algorithm even though each query reveals only one noisy gradient.

descriptionHtml:
Third-Order Smooth Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization

We seek an approximate stationary point of a possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. Its first three derivatives are globally Lipschitz, and the gap between the starting value and the infimum is bounded. At each query x∈E, the oracle uses a fresh independent sample to return an unbiased estimate of ∇f(x) with uniformly bounded variance. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E satisfying E[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε, where the expectation includes both oracle and algorithm randomness.

The underlying minimization problem is infx∈Ef(x). The algorithm receives E with its Borel σ-algebra, the measurable sample space Ω, the starting point x0∈E, the smoothness constants L1,L2,L3>0, the noise bound σ≥0, the initial gap bound Δ≥0, and ε. We write ∥⋅∥ for the inner product norm and ∥⋅∥op for the induced operator and multilinear norms.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness through third order). The function f is three times continuously differentiable. For all x,y∈E, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L1∥x−y∥,∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤L2∥x−y∥,∥∇3f(x)−∇3f(y)∥op≤L3∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Initial objective gap). The starting point satisfies f(x0)−infx∈Ef(x)≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic gradient oracle). On call k at any query x∈E, the oracle returns g(x,ξk), where g:E×Ω→E is jointly measurable. The samples (ξk)k≥0 are independent random variables with common law μ on Ω, and the sample sequence is independent of the algorithm’s randomness. For every fixed x∈E and ξ∼μ, the vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable, the squared error ∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable, and Eξ∼μ[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼μ[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σ2.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable under the joint randomness of the algorithm and the sample sequence. Its gradient norm must be integrable under this law and satisfy E[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
On a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, f∈C3 is nonconvex in general, with L1-Lipschitz gradient, L2-Lipschitz Hessian and L3-Lipschitz third derivative. The initial gap satisfies f(x0)−inff≤Δ. Each query uses a fresh IID sample from a jointly measurable unbiased gradient oracle with variance at most σ2. The target is a measurable output x^ with E∥∇f(x^)∥≤ε. Here Li,ε>0 and Δ,σ≥0.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L₁ : ℝ
  L₂ : ℝ
  L₃ : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE Params.measurableE Params.borelE
  Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L₁ ∧ 0 < q.L₂ ∧ 0 < q.L₃ ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (μ : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (μ : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, x) ω => g x ω } ∧
      ContDiff ℝ 3 f ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ q.L₁ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) y‖ ≤ q.L₂ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (gradient f)) x - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (gradient f)) y‖ ≤
        q.L₃ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x, f q.x0 - f x ≤ q.Δ) ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (g x) (μ : Measure _)) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂(μ : Measure _) = gradient f x) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2) (μ : Measure _)) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2 ∂(μ : Measure _) ≤ q.σ ^ 2)
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex
